issue_context.title: `explode` on empty list misaligns columns
issue_context.body:
#### What language are you using?
Python
#### Have you tried latest version of polars?
yes
#### What version of polars are you using?
0.13.55

#### What operating system are you using polars on?
Linux Mint 20.3

#### What language version are you using
python 3.10.4
#### Describe your bug.
When a column of lists contains an empty list, `explode` misaligns the columns.

#### What are the steps to reproduce the behavior?
Starting with this data:
```python
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({
    "b": [[1], [2], []] * 2,
}).with_row_count()
df
```
```
shape: (6, 2)
┌────────┬───────────┐
│ row_nr ┆ b         │
│ ---    ┆ ---       │
│ u32    ┆ list[i64] │
╞════════╪═══════════╡
│ 0      ┆ [1]       │
├╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┼╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┤
│ 1      ┆ [2]       │
├╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┼╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┤
│ 2      ┆ []        │
├╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┼╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┤
│ 3      ┆ [1]       │
├╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┼╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┤
│ 4      ┆ [2]       │
├╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┼╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┤
│ 5      ┆ []        │
└────────┴───────────┘
```
An `explode` on `b` will misalign columns.
```python3
df.explode(['b'])
```

```
>>> df.explode(['b'])
shape: (6, 2)
┌────────┬──────┐
│ row_nr ┆ b    │
│ ---    ┆ ---  │
│ u32    ┆ i64  │
╞════════╪══════╡
│ 0      ┆ 1    │
├╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┼╌╌╌╌╌╌┤
│ 1      ┆ 2    │
├╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┼╌╌╌╌╌╌┤
│ 2      ┆ null │
├╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┼╌╌╌╌╌╌┤
│ 3      ┆ 1    │
├╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┼╌╌╌╌╌╌┤
│ 5      ┆ 2    │
├╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┼╌╌╌╌╌╌┤
│ 5      ┆ null │
└────────┴──────┘
```
Notice that `row_nr` 4 disappears, and `row_nr` 5 is duplicated.

The correct result should be:
```
>>> df.explode(['b']).drop('row_nr').with_row_count()
shape: (6, 2)
┌────────┬──────┐
│ row_nr ┆ b    │
│ ---    ┆ ---  │
│ u32    ┆ i64  │
╞════════╪══════╡
│ 0      ┆ 1    │
├╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┼╌╌╌╌╌╌┤
│ 1      ┆ 2    │
├╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┼╌╌╌╌╌╌┤
│ 2      ┆ null │
├╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┼╌╌╌╌╌╌┤
│ 3      ┆ 1    │
├╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┼╌╌╌╌╌╌┤
│ 4      ┆ 2    │
├╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌┼╌╌╌╌╌╌┤
│ 5      ┆ null │
└────────┴──────┘
```
#### Test Case
```python
df = pl.DataFrame({"b": [[1], [2], []] * 2}).with_row_count()

pl.testing.assert_frame_equal(
    df.explode(['b']),
    df.explode(['b']).drop('row_nr').with_row_count()
)
```
```
>>> pl.testing.assert_frame_equal(
...     df.explode(['b']),
...     df.explode(['b']).drop('row_nr').with_row_count()
... 
... )
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "/home/corey/.virtualenvs/PolarsIssue3.10/lib/python3.10/site-packages/polars/testing.py", line 139, in assert_frame_equal
    _assert_series_inner(
  File "/home/corey/.virtualenvs/PolarsIssue3.10/lib/python3.10/site-packages/polars/testing.py", line 245, in _assert_series_inner
    raise_assert_detail(
  File "/home/corey/.virtualenvs/PolarsIssue3.10/lib/python3.10/site-packages/polars/testing.py", line 266, in raise_assert_detail
    raise AssertionError(msg)
AssertionError: DataFrame are different

Value mismatch
[left]:  [5]
[right]: [4]
```
#### Other Notes
I found this while testing two answers for this [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/73061008/is-there-a-polars-function-to-dot-product-two-lists) question.  The OP states that they are concerned about RAM, so I designed two performant -- and yet RAM-saving -- solutions.  This bug arose as I was attempting to benchmark against a simple `explode` solution, in terms of wall-clock and maximum RAM.
comments: Thanks a lot for the report @cbilot. A fix is coming up.

Thanks, I was finally able to benchmark my two solutions to the [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/73061008/is-there-a-polars-function-to-dot-product-two-lists) question.  It turns out that using `explode` on the lists performs quite well.   (And the two solutions perform about 4-5x faster than using `apply` and `numpy.dot`.)

I also wanted to show how to use `slice` to get great Polars performance in cases where memory pressure is an issue.
